The frontend regression covers both languages with simulated unavailable connector/ability dispatch and absent author capabilities. This is a local PHP double, not a live frontend certification.

The original failed preflight identity, payloads and operation derivation remain immutable. The active verification binding accepts only the explicitly reviewed original-to-final candidate transition.

The exact original private journal bytes are preserved and checked. Both original operations are reconciled before any same-operation retry or peer submission; unknown, conflicting or changed outcomes stop mutation.
Truthful initial pending/absent observations remain intact. Final current-runtime saved readbacks and exact source-bound preview artifacts determine completed preflight validity.
The permit preserves mandatory immutable content, source-bound actual preview, readiness and fresh capacity checks; recovery does not open hourly publication gates.

Recognized global outages stop the remaining queue and create a persistent cooldown scoped to the execution context and exact current runtime binding. Reopening the state store preserves the deadline.

Known request timeout, rate limit, server error, connection/body-read failure, incomplete chunked read, bridge timeout and connector errors retain safe typed handling. The standard Retry-After delta/date is sanitized; a missing or invalid hint uses the conservative fallback.
A submitted mutation with an uncertain response remains ambiguous. Transport code performs no automatic HTTP retry or POST replay; recovery after the cooldown reconciles the original operation.
A cooldown blocks controlled first publication before its capacity receipt is consumed.

Article-local content defects and known absence/conflicts retain local classification. Already-published checkpoints survive public verification outages and resume fresh QA without publication replay.

Only the exact observed usage notice may be removed from the end of one text block, followed by full JSON parsing. Unknown prose, HTML wrappers, duplicate notices, invalid counts, truncation and explicit errors remain rejected.
The recovery switch is a duplicate-protected boolean scoped to the preflight command.
